finding.title: Correct or remove program_ref_resolver.dart's false production-integration doc claims
finding.rule: Evans (ubiquitous language / doc-reality drift) + Fowler (speculative generality)

evidence.quote:
/// calendar service. Production wires this to the local calendar engine
/// (DNI-330).

/// Dashboard, scheduler, and reader all consume this same resolver so they
/// agree on which `ContentItem` a calendar entry points to (FR16).

finding.why: Two present-tense claims in this class's doc comment don't match the codebase. (1) 'Production wires this to the local calendar engine (DNI-330)' — docs/planning/epics.md:782 records DNI-330 as Story 25.9, 'core/labels/ rebuild — three new modes, ContentIndex consumer, static API deleted', unrelated to calendar-engine wiring. (2) 'Dashboard, scheduler, and reader all consume this same resolver' — scheduler_providers.dart:108 calls index.lookup() directly, bypassing ProgramRefResolver's whitespace/transliteration normalization entirely. Repo-wide grep for ProgramRefResolver(/ProgramRefSource confirms zero call sites outside this file and one story-acceptance test — the class is fully built, fully unit-tested, and has never been wired into any consumer. Whether the ad-hoc direct lookups in scheduler/dashboard/reader ever actually disagree (a live FR16 violation) is unverified — the calendar rows may be pre-canonicalized at seed time, which would make runtime resolution unnecessary in practice; that needs runtime/data confirmation, not just this static read.
finding.recommendation: Either wire the named consumers (starting with scheduler_providers.dart:108) through ProgramRefResolver.resolve() so the FR16 claim is true, or rewrite the doc comment to state plainly that it isn't wired yet and cite the real tracking ticket (not DNI-330).
acceptance_criteria: program_ref_resolver.dart's doc comment cites an accurate ticket for production wiring, or states it is not yet wired.
If FR16 sharing is the intended design, at least scheduler_providers.dart's calendar-derived ref lookups route through ProgramRefResolver instead of a raw index.lookup().

finding.title: Fix ContentTree.parent()'s off-by-one when a leaf precedes its container in source order
finding.rule: Correctness bug (Fowler duplicated-but-inconsistent logic between pass 1 and pass 2)
finding.why: Empirically verified: constructed a 4-level Bavli fixture where the leaf item ('Berakhot 2a:1') appears before its own container ('Berakhot 2a') in the input list, called ContentTree.fromCurricula(...).parent('Berakhot 2a:1'), and got 'Berakhot 2' (the grandparent/daf-level container) instead of the correct immediate parent 'Berakhot 2a'. Root cause: for a leaf, `_ancestorLevels(item)` already returns the PARENT container's own key (that's its documented purpose, and pass 1 at lines 110-121 uses it directly with no further truncation). Pass 2 treats `levels` uniformly as if it were the item's own key and applies a second `.sublist(0, length - 1)` 'walk up one level' step — which, for leaves, walks up an extra level past the true parent. Pass 1 resolves leaves correctly when their container is registered first; pass 2's fallback only fires — with the wrong answer — when a leaf is encountered before its container. ContentTree.parent() currently has zero callers in lib/ (content_hierarchy_screen.dart uses only .children()/.containerFor()), so this is not live-user-visible today, but it is a public, documented, keepAlive-cached API on the exact class whose stated purpose is 'O(1) parent/child/adjacent traversal' — the first feature that calls .parent() for breadcrumb 'up' navigation inherits a silently-wrong result whenever source ordering isn't strictly parent-before-child.
finding.recommendation: In pass 2's leaf branch, use `ancestorLevels` (the value already returned by _ancestorLevels) directly as the parent container key, the same way pass 1 does — do not apply an additional sublist(0, length-1) truncation for leaves.
acceptance_criteria: A regression test at test/core/content/content_tree_test.dart builds a curriculum with a leaf listed before its own container and asserts ContentTree.parent(leafRef) returns the immediate parent, not the grandparent.
Existing epic_25_schema_core_test.dart ContentTree assertions continue to pass.

finding.title: Remove or wire up HierarchyBrowserState's unused currentPath/canGoBack public getters
finding.why: Both are documented as 'Public API for external callers' reachable via the widget's GlobalKey, but the sole caller (HierarchySelectionPanel) never accesses `_browserKey.currentState?.currentPath` or `.canGoBack` — only `.navigateBack()` and `.clearNavigation()` are ever invoked through the key. The caller instead maintains its own parallel `_navigationStack`/`canGoBack` state fed via the onNavigationChanged callback, duplicating the same information HierarchyBrowserState already tracks internally.
finding.recommendation: Delete the two unused getters (and their doc-comment mention) unless a near-term caller is planned; if HierarchySelectionPanel's parallel navigation-stack tracking is meant to be temporary, replace it with these getters instead of keeping both.
acceptance_criteria: No lib/ reference to HierarchyBrowserState.currentPath or .canGoBack exists, or a real caller uses them in place of a duplicate local navigation stack.

finding.title: Replace awaited per-row insert/update loops with Drift batch() in curriculum_scope_dao, stage_dao, and track_dao.purgeHistory

evidence.quote:
for (final value in scopeValues) {
        await into(curriculumScopes).insert(

for (final stage in stages) {
        await insertStageDefinition(stage);

for (final stage in stages) {
        await insertStageDefinition(stage);

finding.why: These four loops are all already inside a db.transaction() (so DB-2 is satisfied — no partial-write risk), but each issues N sequential awaited statements where Drift's batch() would send one. track_dao.purgeHistory is the worst case: on 'delete and wipe history' for a track with hundreds of completions, it round-trips once per row to stamp purgedAt instead of one batched UPDATE. The three sites from the companion DB-2 finding (point_config_dao.seedDefaults, study_day_config_dao.seedDefaults, track_learning_order_dao.upsertOrder) share the identical pattern and compound this once they're wrapped in a transaction.
finding.recommendation: Convert each loop to `batch((b) { for (...) { b.insert(...)/b.update(...); } })`, which Drift supports for both inserts and per-row updates with distinct WHERE clauses inside one batch call.
acceptance_criteria: curriculum_scope_dao.setScopes, stage_dao.replaceStagesForTrack/replaceStagesForCurriculum, and track_dao.purgeHistory's tombstone step use batch() instead of a per-row await loop.
Existing tests for these methods pass unchanged (behavior-preserving refactor).

finding.title: Split completion_dao.dart, points_balance_dao.dart, track_dao.dart, and completion_dao_extended_test.dart under the 400-line AG-3 cap
finding.why: All four are more than 2x the 400-line hand-written-file cap. completion_dao.dart mixes cross-profile-scope-guarded reads, raw-SQL tier filtering, and grouped aggregates in one file; points_balance_dao.dart mixes balance/ledger/redemption CRUD with sync-outbox plumbing; track_dao.dart mixes lifecycle CRUD with two different multi-table transactional delete flows. Long files raise the odds that the next edit misses a nearby invariant (e.g. the DB-3 loop found in track_dao.dart's purgeHistory, buried 400 lines in).
finding.recommendation: Split by responsibility, e.g. completion_dao.dart into a read/aggregate DAO plus a cross-profile-guarded companion; points_balance_dao.dart into balance+ledger vs redemption vs sync-enqueue helpers; track_dao.dart into lifecycle CRUD vs the two delete/purge transactional flows.
acceptance_criteria: A Rule-0 line-count check (e.g. `find lib -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400'`) is added to `make audit` and passes.
